newsitem.title: FINLAND: FOCUS - Merita Bank profit surges.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Merita Bank profit surges.

text.p: Finland's largest banking group Merita Oy on Thursday reported a 93 percent jump in January-September earnings and said that shareholders would enjoy a dividend for the first time in five years.

Operating profits after credit losses rose to 930 million markka ($203.5 million) from 482 million. The result matched analysts' expectations and further confirmed that the Finnish banking sector is recovering from the deep crisis of the early 1990s.
"This was a very healthy profit," said broker Jukka Leppa of Arctos Securities.

Merita attributed the earnings growth to a significant decline in non-performing loans and credit losses, steady performance in its core banking business, increased commissions from securities trading and successful cost control.

The surge in profits meant that shareholders in Merita -- formed by the 1995 merger of banking groups Unitas and Kansallis-Osake-Pankki KOPF.HE -- could expect a dividend for the first time in five years.
"It is our aim that the result for 1996 will permit us to resume payment of dividend," the bank said.
"We see good possibilities for improving profitability of the bank," Merita CEO Vesa Vainio told Reuters Financial Television (RFTV).
On the Helsinki Stock Exchange, Merita's A share initially rose on the news to 14.20 markka but then eased to 13.60 in steady trade, down 0.20 markka from Wednesday's close of 13.80.
Brokers welcomed the result as a sign of a healthier core banking business. "There were no extraordinary gains... the result wasn't made prettier by share sales," Leppa said.
Merita group net income from financial operations rose to 3,026 million markka from 2,756 million.
Loan losses were down to 1,144 million markka from 1,443 million. "The trend in loan losses has been more favourable than expected," Merita said.
Net income from securities trading grew to 873 million markka from 399 million. Disposals of real estate amounted to 700 million markka, yielding gains of 80 million markka for Merita Real Estate.
Merita said the merger process had progressed as planned or even ahead of schedule and that the full impact of merger-related cost savings would be felt next year.
Merita said that in the longer run, it stands to lose annual revenues of 200-300 million markka if Finland joins the European Economic and Monetary Union, due to start in 1999.
This would come on top of earlier estimated direct transition costs of 200 million markka projected for 1997-2002.
However, Vainio said that in EMU capital markets would deepen, creating business opportunities also for Merita.
"The capital markets will be much deeper for Finns and Finnish banks...so I guess we can get some new revenues also," Vainio told RFTV. ($1=4.57 Markka)
